observations: Photo 0 shows a used turbocharger with compressor housing, turbine housing, inlet pipe, and a yellow tag with illegible text.
Photo 1 shows the turbine/exhaust side of a similar used turbocharger with flanges and piping.
Both photos carry a watermark reading 'DNL EQUIPMENT SALES AND POSTED ON JIJI'.
No readable Caterpillar, C9, part number, or data plate is visible in either photo.

claims.evidence: No Caterpillar or C9 marking is readable in photo 0 or photo 1; only an illegible yellow tag is visible.

risks.proof: Video of the compressor wheel spinning freely by hand, or a borescope view of the wheel and bearings

risks.risk: Not actually a Caterpillar C9 part
risks.proof: Clear photo of the data plate, part number, or casting number
risks.if_unproven: as a generic turbocharger of unknown fitment

risks.proof: Close-up of oil feed and drain ports with shaft play check
Full assembly photo showing all housings, linkages, and bolts

proof_requests: Clear photo of any data plate, tag, or part number on the turbocharger
Video of the compressor wheel spinning freely with no shaft play
Close-up of oil ports and bearing housing
response.reason: The photos show a used turbocharger, so it can be priced at worst case as a non-working generic unit; the Caterpillar C9 claim is unproven and would raise the price only with a readable data plate.
